source: NCERT Class VII, Curiosity: Textbook of Science, Ch. 6.

sections.heading: 1. Adolescence and Puberty
points: **Adolescence** = the stage of life between **childhood and adulthood** (roughly **11 to 18/19 years**), a time of rapid **growth and change**.
**Puberty** = the period when the body becomes capable of **reproduction**; it begins/ends at different ages for different people.
Changes are triggered by **hormones** (chemical messengers) from **endocrine glands**.

sections.heading: 2. Changes at Puberty
points: **Sudden increase in height** (growth spurt) — girls usually mature a little earlier than boys.
**Voice changes** — deeper in boys (larynx grows → 'Adam's apple').
**Skin changes** — more active oil glands → **pimples/acne**; more sweating.
Development of **secondary sexual characteristics** (body shape, body hair, etc.).
**Emotional changes** — new feelings, mood swings, seeking independence.

sections.heading: 3. Hormones and Reproductive Health
points: Reproductive hormones: **testosterone** (male) and **oestrogen** (female).
Other important hormones/glands: **thyroid (thyroxine — needs iodine)**, **pancreas (insulin)**, **adrenal**, **pituitary** (the 'master gland').
**Menstruation** in girls is a normal, healthy process controlled by hormones.
This stage needs **awareness, hygiene and respect** — not shame.

sections.heading: 4. Nutrition, Hygiene and Well-being
points: A **balanced diet** (proteins, iron, calcium, vitamins) supports rapid growth; iron prevents **anaemia**.
**Personal hygiene**, regular **exercise**, adequate **sleep** are important.
**Avoid** tobacco, alcohol and drugs; be aware of **peer pressure**.
A positive, respectful attitude towards one's own and others' changing bodies matters.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Adolescence ≈ 11–19 years; puberty = body becomes capable of reproduction.
Changes driven by hormones (endocrine glands); pituitary = master gland.
Reproductive hormones: testosterone (male), oestrogen (female).
Puberty signs: growth spurt, voice change (boys), acne, secondary sexual characteristics.
Iron-rich balanced diet prevents anaemia; menstruation is normal & healthy.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: Changes at puberty are caused by **hormones** from **endocrine glands**.
**Testosterone = male**, **oestrogen = female** reproductive hormones.
The **pituitary** is the 'master gland'; **thyroxine** (thyroid) needs **iodine**.
Menstruation is a **normal, healthy** process — not something to be ashamed of.
